text:
emma_support: Heads-up — ACME (customer) hitting widespread 429s in prod starting ~2026-03-15T10:00Z. They report minute-aligned spikes, lots of short requests, and immediate Retry-After headers. Can SRE/eng help triage?

acme_ops: Confirming. 429 response headers include `X-RateLimit-Remaining: 0`, `Retry-After: 8`. Traffic pattern: a fleet of workers opening many concurrent streams every minute. Region: eu-west-1, api_key: sk-live-***.

mike_sre: Thanks. Quick questions: are they reusing connections or opening per-request? Do we see identical request IDs or rolling ones? Any client-side retry storm?

acme_ops: They said they upgraded an internal job that spawns ~800 short-lived HTTP/2 streams (okhttp) per minute, no connection pooling, SDK v0.9. Retries are agressive with no jitter. We can reproduce locally.

julia_eng: That pattern explains it: our minute-level quota (TPM/RPM) is enforced at the edge using a fixed-window with burst tokens. Many concurrent short streams can exhaust per-key tokens at the top of the minute even if average throughput is okay. HTTP/2 multiplexing increases concurrency and clusters requests into windows.

emma_support: Requesting reproduction steps and headers: can you capture full response headers including any `X-Request-ID` and `X-RateLimit-*` or `X-RW-*` fields and paste a small curl that reproduces the spike?

acme_ops: Repro snippet:```bash
for i in {1..800}; do curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-live-***" \ 
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ 
  --http2-prior-knowledge \ 
  -d '{"prompt":"ping"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate &
done; wait
```They see many 200s, then a wall of 429s with `x-rate-limit-remaining: 0`.

mike_sre: Ok. Immediate mitigations for the customer: 1) Reuse connections (keep-alive). Opening new TCP/TLS for every request multiplies our edge load. 2) Limit max concurrent streams per connection (okhttp: set `maxRequests`/`maxRequestsPerHost`). 3) Add exponential backoff with full jitter on 429s. 4) Add client-side pacing to spread requests across the minute.

julia_eng: From infra side we can: a) inspect the per-key RPM/TPM chart in Console -> Usage -> Rate limits for that key, b) search edge logs for `request_id` to confirm fixed-window bucket exhaustion, c) check if the requests hit the same edge node which could cause localized bursting.

mike_sre: Commands to help triage:```bash
# get recent throttle events for key
kubectl logs -l app=rate-limiter -n prod --since=2h | grep "sk-live-***" | tail -n 200
# query edge traces by request id
rg "request_id=" /var/log/edge/*.log | head
```Those will show the throttle reason (rpm vs tpm) and window boundaries.

acme_ops: We can throttle client to 200 concurrent and add 100ms jitter between each request. Will try now.

emma_support: Also ask them to surface `X-RateLimit-*` headers when they log 429s — that tells us which rule tripped. If header missing, note it and we can enable debug headers temporarily.

julia_eng: Long-term fixes/options: 1) Add client token-bucket pacing so they never send more than N requests/minute; 2) Move heavy fan-out jobs to background and spread across seconds; 3) If they need sustained high RPM, consider Dedicated capacity or request a quota increase (require business review).

mike_sre: For immediate testing we can give a short-lived lift: apply a 5-minute emergency bump of +30% RPM to their key in staging so they can validate changes. Need ops approval.

oncall_bot: Incident created: INC-2026-1803. Owner: @mike_sre. Priority: P2.

emma_support: Thanks @acme_ops. Please paste their logs after trying the client-side mitigations. If 429s persist, we'll coordinate a temporary quota bump while they implement retries/connection pooling. :thumbsup:

acme_ops: Update: after limiting concurrent streams to 150 and adding jitter, 429s dropped to near zero in a 30m run. One or two stray 429s still appear at minute boundaries but much better.

mike_sre: Great — that confirms fixed-window exhaustion. We'll keep monitoring. Follow-ups: - Ops to decide on temporary bump if they need smooth rollout - Eng docs: add guidance on HTTP/2 stream limits and SDK defaults.

julia_eng: I'll add an entry to the SDK migration guide: "Avoid per-request connection churn; prefer long-lived connections + client-side rate limiter." Will also propose exposing per-key sliding-window smoothing option in the future.

emma_support: Closing loop: created ticket RW-3819 to update docs + offer onboarding for Dedicated/quota discussions. Thanks everyone.
